title: Stopping early with break
idea: TOOL: once found, you can stop searching with break — no need to check the rest. Predict behaviour.

exercises.prompt:
Predict the output:

nums = [3, 8, 8, 1]
target = 8
found = False
for n in nums:
    if n == target:
        found = True
        break
print(found)
exercises.explanation: The first 8 sets found to True and break stops the loop. The answer is still True — you found it.

exercises.prompt: Why use break after setting found = True?
options: once you know it is present, checking the rest is wasted work
exercises.explanation: A yes/no only needs ONE match. break stops early so you do not scan items you no longer need to check.

exercises.prompt: Adding break after a match does not change WHETHER the value was found — only how soon you stop.
exercises.explanation: found is already True before break. break just ends the loop early; the yes/no answer is the same.
break ends the loop immediately. With a yes/no search, one match is enough to stop.
2 is the second item; it sets found True and break stops. The message is 'present'.

exercises.prompt: If the target is NOT in the list, what does break do?
options: nothing — break only runs on a match, which never happens, so the loop finishes normally
it stops the loop at the start
exercises.explanation: break is inside the if, so with no match it never runs. The loop checks every item and found stays False.
Flag starts False, loop compares each item, and on a match you set True and break out early.

exercises.prompt: With break, a search can finish before reaching the end of the list.
exercises.explanation: As soon as it finds the target it breaks out, so it need not visit the remaining items.

exercises.prompt:
Predict the output:

nums = [1, 2, 3]
target = 9
found = False
for n in nums:
    if n == target:
        found = True
        break
print(found)
exercises.explanation: 9 is absent, so the if never runs, break never runs, and found stays False after the full scan.

exercises.prompt: For a plain yes/no search, break is...
options: a nice speed-up, since one match is all you need
required or the code is wrong
a way to change the answer
exercises.explanation: break is optional but efficient: the answer cannot change once found is True, so you may as well stop.
